author: Benita Kolovos and Stephanie Convery
description:
Premier steps down from top job ahead of expected spill, saying her deputy has her ‘unqualified support’

  • Live updates: Jacinta Allan quits as premier of Victoria

  • Who is Ben Carroll?

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian premier, Jacinta Allan, has announced her resignation from the top job, after a tumultuous 48 hours for
title: Jacinta Allan resigns as Victorian premier ahead of leadership challenge by Ben Carroll

author: Dan Jervis-Bardy Chief political correspondent and Nick Visser
description:
Secretary and president of Australian Council of Trade Unions announced surprise departures on Monday evening

The leadership of the trade union movement is set for a major shakeup after the secretary and president of the Australian Council of Trade Unions announced their surprise departures.

The ACTU’s secretary, Sally McManus, and its president, Michele O’Neil, revealed on Monday night they would be stepping down after eight years together. Anthony Albanese described both as personal friends and “giants of the labour movement”.

Continue reading...
title: PM praises Sally McManus and Michele O’Neil as ‘giants’ as they resign from ACTU

author: Lucy Campbell and Lauren Gambino
description:
Fraught time for Ken Martin as new reporting details cash-flow problem and divisions over party’s direction

Mounting financial pressures and growing internal turmoil at the Democratic National Committee (DNC) have intensified scrutiny of chair Ken Martin, as new reporting detailed a deepening cash-flow problem, management concerns and widening divisions over the party’s direction less than 100 days before the November midterm elections.

The latest reporting has underscored both the committee’s financial distress and the toll it has taken on Martin personally. The New York Times reported that the embattled DNC chair, who took the helm last year, became the subject of an internal HR inquiry after throwing his phone in the direction of a junior aide’s desk during a heated exchange in early July, prompting a formal complaint. The Times, citing people familiar with the matter, also rep
title: DNC chair faces growing scrutiny amid financial pressure and internal turmoil

author: George Chidi
description:
Defense department updated database of casualties to list four service members deceased in ‘Overseas Operations’

A controversial move by the Pentagon to reclassify casualties in the Iran war is being taken by US military veterans as a sign of disrespect for the dead.

“It’s such a huge disrespect for the families,” said Michael E Smith, a retired US rear admiral and the founder of National Security Leaders for America. “To claim that they weren’t killed as a result of the war – oh, it was just overseas operations – is just ludicrous.”

Continue reading...
title: Trump administration’s revision of Iran war casualties ‘huge disrespect’, say veterans

author: Peter Walker and Josh Halliday
description:
PM wants curriculums for students aged 14 and above to be more responsive to local jobs market

Andy Burnham will tell schools across England to adapt their curriculums to the needs of local businesses as part of a devolution drive aimed at tackling the jobs crisis for young people.

By moving decision-making to local areas, the PM hopes the plan will make technical and vocational skills as valued as academic qualifications – and help cut the benefits bill.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham to tell schools in England to adapt teaching to local business needs

author: Sinéad Campbell
description:
Green party leader shared picture of man wearing T-shirt with words ‘we’re only making plans for Nigel’ alongside a guillotine

Police are “conducting inquiries” into an image shared by Green party leader Zack Polanski on Instagram after Reform UK reported it for “inciting murder”.

The image showed a man wearing a black T-shirt with the words “we’re only making plans for Nigel”, alongside a photograph of a guillotine.

Continue reading...
title: Police make inquiries after Farage reports Polanski post for ‘inciting murder’

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Prime minister pays tribute to secretary and president of the Australian Council of Trade Unions after surprise announcement. Follow updates live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

In a statement, the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, described Sally McManus and Michele O’Neil as personal friends and “giants of the labour movement”.

He said:

Working families are in a stronger financial position today than they would otherwise be because of the tireless advocacy and strong leadership of Sally McManus and Michele O’Neil.

Sally and Michele secured incredible successes for working people in their eight years together leading Australia’s union movement – the firs
title: Australia news live: Anthony Albanese praises Sally McManus and Michele O’Neil as ‘giants’ as they step down from ACTU

author: Alexandra Topping
description:
Former education secretary will take up influential role that puts her at vanguard of Labour’s battle to win next general election

Bridget Phillipson has been appointed Labour party chair, putting her at the vanguard of Labour’s battle to win the next general election.

The former education secretary and architect of a landmark overhaul in special education needs (Send) provision in England will follow in the footsteps of other Labour big beasts who have held the position, including Harriet Harman, Angela Rayner and Tom Watson.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham appoints Bridget Phillipson as Labour party chair

author: Sam Levin in Los Angeles
description:
David Huerta was arrested while protesting against an ICE operation during crackdown in Los Angeles

The Department of Justice has moved to dismiss charges against a prominent California union leader who was arrested while protesting against an immigration raid in Los Angeles last year, in the latest US government case against protesters to fall apart.

David Huerta, the president of Service Employees International Union United Service Workers West, was arrested at a June 2025 demonstration and has been fighting the charges ever since. On Monday, the US attorney’s office in LA filed a motion to dismiss the charges against him.

Continue reading...
title: US justice department dismisses charges against California union leader

author: Associated Press
description:
Los Angeles prosecutors give detailed account of Celeste Rivas Hernandez’s last night

Prosecutors on Monday gave a moment-by-moment account of the last night of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez, showing that after a stream of text messages with the singer D4vd, her phone went permanently silent when she arrived at his home.

The texts were shown in court on the fifth and probably final day of a Los Angeles hearing to determine whether he will go to trial in her killing.

Continue reading...
title: Court told of slain girl’s final texts as she approached singer D4vd’s home

author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
description:
New prime minister wants to focus at home, but his first week already suggests the world has other plans

It took just seven days in office for Andy Burnham to meet his first world leader. As he welcomed Volodymyr Zelenskyy to a naval base in Portsmouth on Monday, the new prime minister told the Ukrainian president it was “no accident” he was his first international visitor since entering No 10.

“It is intended to send a very clear message,” Burnham told him. “We are with Ukraine 100%, I am personally with you 100%, and I will honour every commitment this country has made to Ukraine in full.” In short, the UK’s support for Kyiv would continue despite the change in leadership.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham’s Ukraine gambit is a symbolic start for PM who wants to look inward

author: Priya Bharadia
description:
Robert Bush, owner of Legacy Independent Funeral Directors, left bodies ‘rotting away’, family members say

A fraudulent funeral director broke the trust of families on an “almost industrial scale” as their loved ones’ bodies were left “rotting away”, a court has heard.

Robert Bush, owner of Legacy Independent Funeral Directors in Hull, appeared at Hull crown court on Monday for a five-day sentencing hearing. He previously pleaded guilty to 67 offences, including 30 counts of preventing lawful and decent burial.

Continue reading...
title: Hull funeral director broke families’ trust on ‘almost industrial scale’, court hears

author: Gaya Gupta
description:
Julie Masino faced criticism as restaurant chain was called ‘woke’ and ‘soulless’ after unveiling modernized logo

Cracker Barrel’s CEO, Julie Masino, is stepping down, the restaurant announced on Monday, nearly a year after the company was swept into a political maelstrom over proposed modernizations to its branding.

Critics on social media denounced the Tennessee-based rustic restaurant chain as “woke” as well as “sterile and soulless” after it unveiled an updated logo that removed Uncle Herschel, the overall-clad man leaning against a barrel in the restaurant’s original logo, last August. Donald Trump weighed in on the updates soon after, posting: “WTF is wrong with Cracker Barrel?!” and demanding on social media that the company “admit a mistake”.
title: Cracker Barrel CEO to step down after overseeing logo backlash last year

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
PM promises lasting solution for England but Tories rule out backing changes funded by tax rises or borrowing

Andy Burnham has pledged to work collaboratively with other parties to find a lasting solution on social care, though the Conservatives have ruled out backing changes funded by tax rises or borrowing.

Senior Labour and Liberal Democrat figures have privately cast doubt on Burnham’s ability to find a cross-party consensus on social care reform in England, given the terms of the Tories’ participation.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham seeks cross-party agreement on future of social care

author: PA Media
description:
Judge quashes Enfield council’s decision to grant planning permission for new women’s and girls’ football academy

A council’s decision to allow Tottenham Hotspur Football Club to build a new training facility in a park in north London has been quashed by a judge at the high court.

The campaign group Guardians of Whitewebbs told a hearing in June that Enfield council’s decision to grant planning permission for a new women’s and girls’ football academy on 6.5 hectares (16 acres) of land in Whitewebbs Park was unlawful.

Continue reading...
title: Spurs’ plans for new training facility in London park blocked by high court

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Appointment of three ministerial aides is first time members of Labour’s most leftwing faction have held government positions

Andy Burnham has appointed three new ministerial aides from Labour’s most leftwing faction, the first time members of the Socialist Campaign Group have been part of the government.

The new chief whip, Anneliese Midgley, has also promised MPs that the government will beef up the role of ministerial aides – known as parliamentary private secretaries (PPSs) – who traditionally go under the radar, allowing them to do more media appearances, take on parliamentary roles and contribute more directly to policy direction.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham brings members of Socialist Campaign Group into government

author: Robyn Vinter
description:
With large areas still burning, damage from national park’s worst blaze could take decades, if not longer, to put right

It is the jewel in the crown of the Highlands, one of Scotland’s most impressive natural landscapes, but 12 days on from the start of an enormous wildfire that is tearing through moorland and forest, the Cairngorms national park is unrecognisable.

Hectares of blackened land were visible as low cloud cleared on Sunday, with smoke billowing into the air from large areas still ablaze. In the evening, the sky glowed an eerie orange.

Continue reading...
title: Swathes of Cairngorms unrecognisable after 12 days of ‘cataclysmic’ wildfires

author: Geraldine McKelvie
description:
Torbitt admits to two counts of fraud by false representation in relation to his parliamentary expenses

A GB News pundit has admitted fraud in relation to his parliamentary expenses when he was a Labour aide.

Matthew Torbitt, a prominent political commentator who once described himself as “Britain’s favourite lefty”, pleaded guilty to two counts of fraud by false representation at a hearing at Thames magistrates court on Monday.

Continue reading...
title: GB News pundit Matthew Torbitt pleads guilty to fraud while Labour aide

author: Damien Gayle
description:
Temperatures up to 35C forecast, triggering heat health alerts and pleas to take care in parched parks and rural areas

Paramedics and firefighters are braced for emergencies across the country this week after UK forecasters predicted a fourth heatwave of the year.

Temperatures are forecast to reach as high as 35C by Wednesday, triggering heat health alerts and an appeal from fire chiefs to take care in parched parks and rural areas.

Continue reading...
title: Britain braces for fourth heatwave of year as fire chiefs issue public appeal

author: Josh Butler
description:
Exclusive: Resurfaced comments by the One Nation leader underline her criticism of paid family violence leave and domestic violence support groups

Pauline Hanson told a podcast last year she believed “your employer should not be responsible” for providing paid domestic violence leave, while her colleague Malcolm Roberts recently referred to the family court as the “slaughterhouse of the nation”, in the latest One Nation comments critical of the family law system to emerge.

Hanson claimed on a 2021 podcast that domestic violence was being “used as a weapon” in court proceedings, and criticised domestic violence groups for focusing on support for women.

Continue reading...
title: Pauline Hanson and Malcolm Roberts deride family law system, calling DV a ‘weapon’ and court a ‘slaughterhouse’

author: Anne Davies
description:
The NSW anti-corruption watchdog has begun a public inquiry into allegations of branch stacking, illegal donations, and interference with preselections

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

If you ever thought branch stacking was a harmless game played by young, ambitious political operatives seeking to advance within the party, think again.

On Monday, on the first day of the corruption watchdog’s inquiry into operation Rosny, an investigation into allegations of “possible offences under the Electoral Funding Act”, we heard boasts on secret tape recordings from a developer that he had “my hands on the state government” and he had “fucked” the career of a state politician by “taking his seat”. As for the state’s building co
title: Secret tape recordings and ‘sham’ payments: the Liberals’ internal ideological war laid bare

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
In his memoir, the former Qantas chief executive denies using the lounge as a tool to influence politicians

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Judges, politicians, newspaper editors and big spenders: Alan Joyce, the former Qantas chief executive, has revealed how the airline admits members to its
title: So how do you get access to the Qantas chairman’s lounge? Alan Joyce has some tips

author: Steven Morris
description:
Gibraltar-based Ros Astengo inspired four men to report sexual assaults carried out by Allan Grimson in 1990s

Ros Astengo, a journalist based in Gibraltar who usually focuses on politics and social issues, had qualms when she began investigating the case of the suspected serial killer Allan Grimson as he neared release from prison after serving more than 20 years.

She worried that she might reopen the scars of survivors of Grimson – but also that she could be putting herself in the “crosshairs” of a dangerous man who had sexually assaulted and battered two young men to death in the late 1990s when he was a Royal Navy petty officer.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I knew what he had done to those boys’: murderer to stay in jail after journalist’s fight for justice

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Former rugby star Daniel Adongo allegedly overstayed visa but supporters say he needed mental health help

A former rugby star who became the first Kenyan to play in the NFL, was deported in June for a visa overstay and multiple arrests, according to federal immigration authorities.

Daniel Adongo, 37, spent two seasons as a linebacker for the Indianapolis Colts, playing twice, and was cut in 2015 after facing domestic violence allegations. His visa expired in 2016, but he remained in the US, a press statement from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said.

Continue reading...
title: First Kenyan to play in NFL deported under Trump immigration crackdown

author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
description:
Team to return for euphoric homecoming after winning all-Ireland men’s final against Kerry, ending decades of defeats

The hex is broken, dispelled, banished, and a story that bewitched Ireland for decades has ended in fairytale: Mayo are all-Ireland champions.

Seventy-five years after a supposed curse condemned its Gaelic men’s football team to endless defeat, the county prevailed and uncorked a wave of emotion that engulfed even its rivals.

Continue reading...
title: Mayo beat 75-year-old ‘curse’ to become Gaelic football champions

author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
Both men scheduled to meet Trump at time where US policy towards wars in Iran and Ukraine in state of flux

Benjamin Netanyahu and Volodymyr Zelenskyy are set to arrive in Washington simultaneously with the goal of winning the ear of Donald Trump at pivotal moments in wars affecting their respective countries.

Netanyahu, Israel’s prime minister, and Zelenskyy, the Ukrainian president, will attend Tuesday’s funeral of Lindsey Graham, the former Republican senator for South Carolina, who died suddenly on 11 July and was a close ally of both leaders.

Continue reading...
title: Netanyahu and Zelenskyy to arrive in Washington for Graham funeral – with hopes of winning Trump’s ear

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
David Cifaldi slipped and his pole pierced him in the side, then walked back hours along the route he had climbed

A Montana man walked 10 miles to safety with a trekking pole speared through his torso after a fall during a hiking expedition on the state’s highest mountain.

David Cifaldi slipped on rocks close to the summit of the 12,803ft (3,902 meters) Granite Peak during the hike on 20 July with two friends. He fell on one of his two poles, and “by the time I rolled over, I kind of knew something wasn’t right”, he told CBS news affiliate KVTQ.

Continue reading...
title: Montana man hikes 10 miles to safety after falling on trekking pole

author: Patrick Commins and Dan Jervis-Bardy
description:
Commonwealth and Western Australia to fund study into construction of large-scale petrol refinery as buffer against fuel vulnerability

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s first new oil refinery in 60 years could be built in Western Australia under the Albanese government’s long-term strategy to shield the country from future global oil shocks.

The commonwealth and the WA government will fund a $4m early-stage feasibility study into construction of what would be the country’s third large-scale petrol refinery.

Continue reading...
title: Potential for first Australian oil refinery in 60 years as treasurer braces for inflation from Middle East war

author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
description:
Artificial intelligence firm should provide $100m for cyber defences, says Hugging Face CEO

  • Business live – latest updates

The boss of the startup hacked by an OpenAI agent has called for the investigation into the incident to show “radical transparency”.

Clement Delangue, chief executive of Hugging Face, said the “unprecedented” attack on his business required a similar response.

Continue reading...
title: Boss of startup hacked by rogue OpenAI agent urges ‘radical transparency’ in investigation

author: Ian Sample Science editor
description:
Scientists say decision is blow to UK astronomy as deep space observatory is home to world-leading facilities

Jodrell Bank Observatory, which runs a world-leading network of radio telescopes, is facing closure after the government’s major funder cut support for the facility.

The deep space observatory, which hosts the Grade I-listed Lovell telescope, is prized by astronomers who study galaxies, black holes, star formation, planets beyond the solar system and the afterglow of the big bang.

Continue reading...
title: Jodrell Bank Observatory facing closure after major funder cuts support

author: Jasper Jolly
description:
Europe and US risk being outpaced on innovation, as happened in the car industry, warns Pascal Soriot

AstraZeneca must operate at “Chinese speed” to ensure it doesn’t suffer the fate of the western automotive industry by losing out to more innovative rivals, the drug company’s boss has said.

The FTSE 100 company is watching the rise of China’s pharmaceutical industry closely and collaborating to take drugs to global markets, but its chief executive, Pascal Soriot, said the US and European pharmaceutical sector must focus on increasing the speed of innovation.

Continue reading...
title: AstraZeneca boss urges western drugmakers to move at ‘Chinese speed’

author: Tom Perkins
description:
Coalition says Chemours downplayed health and climate risks in bid to fast-track the compound’s use

A coalition of 17 environmental groups is demanding the Environmental Protection Agency reject a new Pfas that chemical giant Chemours is attempting to fast track for approval for use in cooling datacenters, and would almost certainly pollute regions around the facilities.

In formal comments submitted to the agency, the groups accuse Chemours of using bad science to downplay the chemical’s toxicity and climate risks. Approving Chemours’ application as it is would violate the law, the Earthjustice legal non-profit, a lead author of the comments, wrote.

Continue reading...
title: US environmental groups urge EPA to reject new Pfas to cool datacenters

author: Diane Taylor
description:
Refugee family reunions in limbo, despite Foreign Office saying it is ready get people out of war-torn territory

The Home Office is blocking the evacuation of dozens of women and children from Gaza, despite the Foreign Office saying it is ready to get people out of the war-torn region.

Last September, the Home Office announced it was suspending refugee family reunion applications and that new, more restrictive rules would be announced in the spring. So far there has been no announcement and the process remains suspended.

Continue reading...
title: Home Office blocking evacuation of dozens of women and children from Gaza

author: Jillian Ambrose
description:
KKR and Energy Capital Partners poised to buy firm despite misgivings from founder and biggest shareholders

  • Business live – latest updates

One of the biggest energy businesses listed on the London Stock Exchange has agreed a controversial £5.7bn takeover by private equity, adding to the growing exodus of companies from the UK market.

The US private equity groups KKR and Energy Capital Partners are poised to buy DCC Energy after the company’s board recommended the offer despite misgivings from its founder and biggest shareholders.

Continue reading...
title: DCC, one of FTSE 100’s biggest energy firms, agrees £5.75bn takeover

author: Martin Belam
description:
Eighteen American troops have been killed and 624 wounded since White House launched war on Tehran. Plus, International Cowboy Day in Kenya

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. The US has paused strikes on Iran for a third night as top military officials advised Donald Trump to halt his bombing campaign, and diplomatic negotiations have continued to avoid a return to all-out war. Oil prices fell on Monday as markets responded to the pause in combat. Tehran said on Sunday it would pause what it called “retaliatory” attacks against US allies in the region.

Trump is said to be weighing up diplomatic and military options in the nearly five-month-old conflict. Axios reported o
title: Trump continues pause on Iran strikes as Pentagon reveals higher casualty figures | First Thing

author: Sandra Laville
description:
Experts who helped Burnham draw up Manchester carbon neutral pledge say backtracking would send wrong message amid wildfires and heatwaves

  • Europe wildfires – latest updates

Leading climate scientists who created Greater Manchester’s carbon neutral by 2038 commitment are urging Andy Burnham to unequivocally reject new drilling in the North Sea.

In a letter to the prime minister they said he, as mayor of Greater Manchester, had unveiled one of the UK’s most ambitious local climate programmes that tackled housing, green growth and public transport.</
title: PM urged to uphold climate pledges made as mayor and ban new North Sea oil drilling

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Top House Democrat says US president ‘failed to deliver’ on campaign promises to lower costs and avoid overseas wars

Donald Trump’s Republican party has “nothing to run on” for the congressional midterm elections after the president broke promises to lower costs and avoid starting war overseas, Hakeem Jeffries has said.

The House minority leader, a New York congressman, made those comments on CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday, exactly 100 days from the 3 November midterms, when Jeffries and his fellow Democrats are aiming to take control of the US House and Senate from their Republican opponents.

Continue r
title: Republicans have ‘nothing to run on’ in midterms after Trump failures, Jeffries says

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Performer on trial on six charges of sexually penetrating a 20-year-old woman without consent

A British YouTuber and musician accused of violently raping a fan after a gig never asked his alleged victim if she wanted sex, a court has been told.

Rapper Yung Filly, whose real name is Andrés Felipe Valencia Barrientos, is fighting six charges of sexually penetrating a 20-year-old woman without consent in a Perth hotel room in September 2024.

Continue reading...
title: British YouTuber Yung Filly describes night he met fan in Australian nightclub before allegedly raping her

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Defence secretary Wes Streeting says the country will see a prime minister that ‘runs towards big and difficult issues’

Good morning. Yesterday Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, told Sky News that, while Andy Burnham spent his first week as PM focusing on cost of living issues, this week the public would see “a prime minister that runs towards big and difficult issues rather than runs away from [them]”. Those challenges include reforming social care and, as Peter Walker reports, Burnham has pledged to use “whatever political capital I have” to finally fix the crumbling social care system in England, saying that without rapid action the NHS could effectively collapse.

Burnham was speaking in a 30-minute interview with the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg going out on Panorama tonight. The BBC put the full interview on
title: Tories and Reform UK tell Burnham they will fight any plan to reform adult social care involving tax rises – UK politics live

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
The royal commission into antisemitism and social cohesion is this week examining security arrangements for the Jewish community

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The deputy commissioner of New South Wales Police has pushed back at calls for the private security sector to be armed at Jewish events.

The royal commission into antisemitism and social cohesion has been examining security arrangements for the Jewish community in this block of hearings, with some witnesses lobbying for the
title: NSW police deputy commissioner says letting Jewish security group carry guns could be seen as ‘favouritism’

author: Brendan Wood for MetDesk
description:
Wind and record-breaking heat are fuelling the continent’s explosive fire season, with Spain and France among worst hit

Explainer: what is a ‘fire cloud’, and how have they worsened wildfires in Europe?

A combination of an unusually wet winter, very low rainfall since spring and repeated record-breaking summer heatwaves is likely to explain why wildfires have ignited, spread and resisted control so readily across France and Spain in recent days.

About 90% of wildfires are started by human activity, typically igniting “fine fuels” such as vegetation grass, pine needles, litter and twigs. And recent weather has almost cer
title: Weather tracker: Why Europe’s wildfires are proving so fierce and difficult to stop

author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
description:
Challenges vary from poor transport links to high numbers of people flocking to the area looking for work

When 19-year-old Dejanae set her online job search criteria for the local area, she was shocked at how few options came back. She studied animal science in college but is struggling to find work in the West Midlands.

“It’s hard. You put Dudley, but it’s mainly jobs outside Dudley that come up because there just isn’t much here,” she said. “Even jobs in Birmingham (10 miles away) are difficult because I’m two hours away on a bus, so they don’t even want to consider me.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘They’re anxious about everything’: life for young people seeking work in Dudley and Lewisham

author: Kat Wong
description:
Federal government touts emergency warning alert test as a success and says no approach works 100% of the time

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A blaring emergency warning alert Australians had been warned about was anti-climactic for some – and totally missed by others.

Almost every phone in the country, alongside some smartwatches and tablets, was supposed to let off a loud noise at about 2pm AEST and receive a po
title: For a few seconds, AusAlert blared around parks, libraries and cinemas – but some didn’t get the alert at all

author: Penry Buckley
description:
So-called ‘Reformers’ hosted recruitment functions with speakers including Tony Abbott and Alan Jones

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Senior politicians in the New South Wales Liberal party supported the work of a group of young conservative power brokers who sought to take control of the party and move it towards the right, the corruption watchdog has heard.

The
title: Senior politicians supported young NSW Liberal power brokers trying to shift party to right, corruption watchdog hears

author: Joe Pinner
description:
Research shows AI accounts are gaining millions of views on TikTok by spreading dubious health advice

Misleading health claims online pose a “huge danger to public safety”, experts have warned, after research has shown that AI-generated doctors are gaining millions of views on TikTok by spreading dubious health advice.

The British Medical Association council deputy chair, Dr Emma Runswick, flagged the risks posed by AI accounts that “peddle medical myths and promote so-called miracle cures”.

Continue reading...
title: Misleading AI-generated doctors pose ‘huge danger to public safety’

author: Hettie O'Brien
description:
In today’s newsletter: Across ​the country, a ​younger generation is turning private disillusionment into public defiance​ against a government that once felt untouchable

Good morning. As flames engulfed parts of France and Spain this weekend, in India, the prime minister, Narendra Modi, was trying to put out a very different kind of fire. Thousands of people arrived in Delhi on Saturday to demand the resignation of his education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan. When he stepped down in the early afternoon, the protests turned into a triumphant block party.

But the Cockroach protests that have swept through India this summer are about much more than a single minister. They have humiliated Modi and undermined the indomit
title: Monday briefing: ​How the Cockroach ​protests ​have expose​d the ​cracks in ​India’s government

author: Benita Kolovos and Stephanie Convery
description:
Carroll, who has confirmed he will make a leadership challenge, was elected to parliament in 2012 and says he has always been ambitious

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

In 2023, when then-public transport minister Ben Carroll failed in his surprising bid to secure the leadership of the Victorian Labor party, he told a press conference: “I was always very keen to rise.”

The premier Daniel Andrews had resigned believi
title: Who is Ben Carroll, the man who wants to be Victoria’s next premier?

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Kumanjayi White died after being restrained by plain-clothes police in the lolly aisle of an Alice Springs supermarket

•Warning: This article contains references to Indigenous Australians who have died

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The family of a young Aboriginal man who died after being restrained by police
title: Family of Indigenous man who died in custody launch legal action over decision not to charge police

author: Bethan McKernan
description:
Relaxed rules mean members only have to wear a top to meetings and activities after extensive feedback

Girlguiding has fully redesigned its uniform across all groups for the first time in more than 30 years, with a focus on “self-expression, belonging and confidence”.

The new range, launched on Monday, has relaxed previous rules: Guides, Rainbows, Brownies and Rangers now only have to wear a top to meetings and activities to be considered “in uniform” after feedback from thousands of girls who said they felt “most comfortable” when allowed to wear what they wanted.

Continue reading...
title: Girlguiding redesigns uniforms to put focus on ‘self-expression and confidence’

author: Jordyn Beazley
description:
Judges find in Faruqi’s favour after One Nation leader launched an appeal against judgement she had breached Racial Discrimination Act

A court has upheld the finding that Pauline Hanson engaged in racial discrimination against Mehreen Faruqi when she tweeted the Greens senator should “pack your bags and piss off back to Pakistan”.

The One Nation leader launched the appeal in November, almost a month after Justice Angus Stewart found Hanson engaged in “seriously offensive” and intimidating behaviour against Faruqi in the September 2022 social media post that breached the Racial Discrimination Act.

Continue reading...
title: Pauline Hanson loses bid to overturn Mehreen Faruqi racial discrimination finding

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Airports in England and Wales are likely to lose millions of passengers if third runway goes ahead, DfT economic paper shows

Expanding Heathrow airport will take thousands of jobs from other regions of the UK, including almost 10,000 from the West Midlands alone, according to an analysis of the government’s own forecasts.

An economic paper published by the Department for Transport last month shows that airports in England and Wales are likely to lose millions of passengers if Heathrow builds a third runway, in a significant blow to regional jobs.

Continue reading...
title: Heathrow expansion would take thousands of jobs from other UK regions, report finds
